1	package filetree
2	
3	import (
4		"os"
5		"path/filepath"
6		"strings"
7	
8		"paper-scan-processor/backend/pdf"
9	)
10	
11	// LocalFile describes one local file discovered by ScanLocalRoot. Not every
12	// file is a PDF — non-PDF files (e.g. image scans) are included too, with
13	// IsPDF false and PageCount 0.
14	type LocalFile struct {
15		Path      string `json:"path"`
16		Name      string `json:"name"` // filename including extension
17		SizeBytes int64  `json:"sizeBytes"`
18		IsPDF     bool   `json:"isPdf"`
19		PageCount int    `json:"pageCount"` // only meaningful when IsPDF is true
20		Corrupt   bool   `json:"corrupt"`   // IsPDF true but its page count could not be read
21	}
22	
23	// LocalFileGroup is one folder's worth of files, plus its nested
24	// subfolders. Name is "" only for the root LocalFileGroup returned by
25	// ScanLocalRoot; every subgroup has a real folder name.
26	type LocalFileGroup struct {
27		Name      string           `json:"name"`
28		Files     []LocalFile      `json:"files"`
29		Subgroups []LocalFileGroup `json:"subgroups"`
30	}
31	
32	// ScanLocalRoot scans root recursively and returns it as a LocalFileGroup:
33	// its own direct files in Files, and every subdirectory (at any depth) as a
34	// nested Subgroups entry. Unlike a subfolder, the root is always returned
35	// even if it's entirely empty, so the UI has something to render a "no
36	// files" state from.
37	func ScanLocalRoot(root string) (LocalFileGroup, error) {
38		return scanDirectory(root, "")
39	}
40	
41	// scanDirectory scans dir's direct entries in a single pass: each file
42	// becomes a LocalFile, each non-hidden subdirectory is scanned recursively
43	// (skipping symlinks) and — if its subtree contains no files at all — is
44	// omitted from Subgroups. name is used as the returned group's Name (pass ""
45	// for the scan root). PDFs whose page count can't be read are still
46	// included, flagged via LocalFile.Corrupt, rather than dropped from the
47	// scan; non-PDF files are never considered corrupt.
48	//
49	// Both slice fields are always initialized to non-nil (even when empty),
50	// since a nil Go slice marshals to JSON `null` rather than `[]`, which
51	// crashes the frontend (e.g. `group.subgroups.length` throws on null).
52	func scanDirectory(dir, name string) (LocalFileGroup, error) {
53		entries, err := os.ReadDir(dir)
54		if err != nil {
55			return LocalFileGroup{}, err
56		}
57	
58		files := []LocalFile{}
59		subgroups := []LocalFileGroup{}
60	
61		for _, e := range entries {
62			entryName := e.Name()
63			if strings.HasPrefix(entryName, ".") {
64				continue
65			}
66	
67			if e.IsDir() {
68				// os.DirEntry.IsDir() reflects the directory entry itself rather
69				// than a resolved symlink target, so a symlinked directory
70				// (including one that would otherwise form a loop) never enters
71				// this branch — it's simply skipped.
72				sub, err := scanDirectory(filepath.Join(dir, entryName), entryName)
73				if err != nil {
74					return LocalFileGroup{}, err
75				}
76				if len(sub.Files) > 0 || len(sub.Subgroups) > 0 {
77					subgroups = append(subgroups, sub)
78				}
79				continue
80			}
81	
82			path := filepath.Join(dir, entryName)
83			info, err := os.Stat(path)
84			if err != nil {
85				continue
86			}
87	
88			isPDF := strings.HasSuffix(strings.ToLower(entryName), ".pdf")
89			var count int
90			var corrupt bool
91			if isPDF {
92				count, err = pdf.PageCount(path)
93				corrupt = err != nil
94			}
95			files = append(files, LocalFile{
96				Path:      path,
97				Name:      entryName,
98				SizeBytes: info.Size(),
99				IsPDF:     isPDF,
100				PageCount: count,
101				Corrupt:   corrupt,
102			})
103		}
104	
105		return LocalFileGroup{Name: name, Files: files, Subgroups: subgroups}, nil
106	}

content.text: Now let me verify it builds and tests pass.

Fixed in `backend/filetree/filetree.go:83-105`: an `os.Stat` failure (e.g. the file vanishing between `ReadDir` and `Stat`, or a permissions issue) previously caused the file to be silently `continue`d out of the scan entirely. message.content: Is it true that this change allows sizeBytes to arrive as null on the frontend?

content.text: No. `SizeBytes` is a plain `int64` (not a pointer, no `omitempty`), so it always marshals to a JSON number — when `info` is nil the fallback `size` variable is just the zero value `0`, which serializes as `0`, not `null`. Only pointer/interface fields (or `omitempty` on certain zero values) can produce `null`/absent JSON in Go, and this field is neither.

description: "Default commit workflow (updated 2026-07-30): show the full drafted commit message (with Co-Authored-By/Claude-Session trailer) in chat for the user to copy-paste into git gui themselves — don't write to GITGUI_MSG (broken by Entire hook) and don't run git commit unless asked"

---

**Current default (updated 2026-07-30):** Don't run `git commit` at all as the default flow. `git add` the relevant paths, draft the full commit message (subject + body + the `Co-Authored-By:`/`Claude-Session:` trailer lines), and print the complete message verbatim in a fenced code block in chat. The user copies it from there and pastes it into git gui's message box themselves, then hits Commit there.

**Why this changed from writing `GITGUI_MSG` (was the default 2026-07-30 through same-day):** This repo has Entire CLI's hooks installed (`.git/hooks/prepare-commit-msg` → `entire hooks git prepare-commit-msg`). When git gui rescans and populates its message box, it runs that hook, which overwrites the message file with its own `Entire-Checkpoint: ...` trailer before git gui reads it — clobbering whatever was written to `GITGUI_MSG`. User confirmed seeing `Entire-Checkpoint: ...` in the box instead of the drafted message. So `GITGUI_MSG` is no longer a reliable handoff channel in this repo; chat is the fallback. If Entire's behavior here ever changes (e.g. it starts preserving existing content, or a config flag suppresses the trailer), the `GITGUI_MSG` approach could be revisited.

**How to apply:** Include the same trailer lines that would otherwise go via `-F`/`-m` (Co-Authored-By, Claude-Session) directly in the printed message so the user can copy the whole block as one paste — don't omit them expecting git gui or a hook to add them.

**When this doesn't apply:** If the user explicitly asks me to run the actual `git commit` (e.g. no git gui in the loop, or a quick one-off), fall back to the older flow below: never commit without explicit confirmation that turn, show the drafted message first, then commit with `-F`.

---

## Older flow (still applies when actually asked to run `git commit` myself)

Never run `git commit` unless the user has explicitly asked for it in this turn. An earlier "commit" instruction does not authorize committing again later in the session — each commit (or batch of commits for one piece of work) needs its own explicit go-ahead. After finishing a reviewable chunk of work, stop and ask whether to commit; don't just do it because that's the rhythm the conversation fell into.

**Why:** User corrected this on 2026-07-02: after saying "commit" once (for Step 2 work), I kept committing on my own for subsequent steps (Step 3a, a test-infra fix, Step 3b) without being asked again each time. This is about the approval relationship with this specific user — a different user of this repo might not want that friction at all — so it belongs in memory, not CLAUDE.md. See [[feedback_memory_vs_claudemd]].

**How to apply:** Finish the work, run verification (build/test/typecheck), summarize what changed, and explicitly ask "want me to commit this?" — then wait. Do not commit proactively even if the previous turn's work was committed after a similar request. This applies within a single session and especially across multiple pieces of work in a row (e.g. a multi-step checklist implementation) — each step's commit needs its own confirmation, not just the first one. See also [[feedback_separate_commits]] for how to split what does get committed once confirmed.

**Show the commit message first (added 2026-07-08):** Even once the user says "commit," show the drafted commit message in the chat turn first, then commit (in that same turn, no extra round-trip needed unless the user objects to the message). Why: user asked to see the message before it's used, so they can review/edit wording before it lands in history.

**Use `git commit -F <file>`, not inline `-m "$(cat <<'EOF' ...)"` (added 2026-07-10):** Draft the message, write it to a scratchpad file with the Write tool, show its contents in chat as the preview, then run `git commit -F <path>`. Why: passing the message inline via a heredoc broke repeatedly whenever the message contained an apostrophe (`picker's`, `it's`) — something outside my own command also wraps the whole shell invocation in single quotes (likely a logging/sandboxing layer doing `eval '<command>'`), and a literal apostrophe anywhere in the text prematurely closes that outer quoting since single quotes can't be escaped from within themselves. Writing the message to a file sidesteps shell quoting entirely — apostrophes, quotes, backticks are all safe in file content. `-F` also naturally satisfies the "show the message first" rule above, since the file is written (and can be shown) before the commit runs. This is purely a workaround for how *I* invoke shell commands in this sandboxed environment — not relevant to a human contributor or a rule about repo content — so it's memory, not CLAUDE.md.

**Skip `git status` / `git add`, pass pathspecs straight to `git commit` (added 2026-07-10):** Default commit command is now `git commit -F <message-file> -- <path1> <path2> ...`, listing exactly the files touched this turn. `git commit <pathspec>` stages and commits only those paths' current working-tree content, regardless of what else is dirty elsewhere — no preceding `git add` needed. `git status` is skippable too since I already know which files I edited from my own tool calls this session; I don't need to discover that via status. Why: user asked for a leaner commit flow after watching the status→add→commit dance every time. Caveat: this repo has had stray unrelated modified files show up before (e.g. `frontend/wailsjs/runtime/*` regenerated by a `wails dev` run outside the session) — always naming explicit paths on `git commit` is what keeps those out, so don't switch to `git commit -a` or `git add -A` even though they'd also skip the status/add dance.
